issues.claim: Обратите внимание на тип параметра `Remove` у `List<int>` и на то, в какой момент метод прекращает поиск.
issues.problem: The second half of the hint ("when the method stops searching") nearly states that Remove stops at the first match, which is the answer hinge. The EN hint has the same strength, so there is no RU/EN drift.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften both hints, e.g. RU: "Обратите внимание на тип параметра `Remove` и на то, сколько элементов метод способен удалить за один вызов." EN: "Look at the parameter type of `Remove` and at how many elements one call can remove."

issues.claim: That is what `RemoveAt(1)` would do: it removes the element at index 1, which is the value `2`.
issues.problem: The resulting list content is right, but `RemoveAt` returns void, so a program using it would not print `True` as option d shows. The explanation also never mentions this.
issues.suggestedFix: Say that the list would end up as `1,1,3` if the element at index 1 were removed, e.g. "The list contents `1,1,3` would result if the element at index 1 (the value `2`) were removed, as `RemoveAt(1)` does. `Remove` takes a value, not an index." Apply the same change to the RU text.

issues.claim: For a `record` the compiler generates `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, the `==` and `!=` operators and an `IEquatable<PointRecord>` implementation based on the field values.
issues.problem: The claim is correct and the sandbox gives `3 1`. However, neither cited page covers the value equality that records generate, and it is half of the answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/record (lang en, kind docs) with matching linkTitles in ru and en.

issues.claim: The same rule applies to `HashSet<T>`, `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` keys, `GroupBy`, `Union` and `Contains`: by default they all rely on `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`.
issues.problem: This is slightly imprecise. `Enumerable.Contains` on an `ICollection<T>` source delegates to that collection's own `Contains`, which may use a different comparer, for example a `HashSet<T>` built with a custom comparer.
issues.suggestedFix: Add "when no comparer is supplied" and note that `Enumerable.Contains` uses the source collection's own `Contains` when the source implements `ICollection<T>`. Apply the same change to the RU explanation.
